clue.text: Earl to mark device for use

parts.note: M stands for the mark, the former German currency
a ploy is a device or stratagem

explanation.surface: A nobleman marks out a gadget he intends to put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To use somebody or something is to put it to work, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Formerly stout model

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
stout and ample both mean large or well-filled

explanation.surface: A model who was once heavily built.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a pattern or instance to follow, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Copper gets tons of conspiracies

parts.note: P is a penny, a coin made of copper or bronze in Britain
tons, informally, means lots

explanation.surface: A police officer uncovers a huge number of conspiracies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is a penny coin, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiracies are secret schemes, synonyms of the plural noun answer.

clue.text: Ended trade organisation that's made too much of

parts.note: something that has ended is over

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of trade are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A defunct trade body that was given more praise than it deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like part of 'trade organisation', a union, but it rearranges TRADE into RATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpraised or overvalued has been made too much of, the past participle sense.

clue.text: Settlement is rejected in warehouse

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the warehouse word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse or warehouse

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: A settlement claim is turned down in a storage building.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a payment or settlement made, as on a purchase, or a sediment that settles.

clue.text: Visionary head of department gets rotary tool

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a reamer is a rotating tool for enlarging holes

explanation.surface: A far-sighted head of department is given a power tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is someone with idealistic, imaginative ideas, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Left in agony? That's evident!

indicators.note: in places the left abbreviation inside the agony word

parts.note: agony is extreme pain

explanation.surface: Someone left suffering is obviously in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain as an adjective means obvious or clear, the same sense as evident.

clue.text: Weaken a club with debts? That's wise?

parts.note: to sag is to weaken or droop
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is wise to undermine a club already in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacious describes someone with keen judgement, a synonym of wise.

clue.text: Claws back pounds, advanced in huge quantities

indicators.note: in places the reversed pair inside the word for huge quantities

parts.note: tons means huge quantities

indicators.note: back means the two pieces that follow are read in reverse order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A firm claws back money that it had lent out in vast sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LA (pounds then advanced) into AL, which goes inside TONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Talons are the hooked claws of a bird of prey, so a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Drunken groom consumed a lot of litres

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so the litres piece goes inside the groom word

parts.note: to groom is to tidy up
DL can be read as a decalitre, ten litres, which is a lot of litres

explanation.surface: A tipsy bridegroom who has put away many litres of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like the bridegroom, but it is the verb meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is British informal for slightly drunk, matching the adjective given.

clue.text: Make good porridge together

parts.note: to atone is to make amends or make good
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, time served

explanation.surface: Instructions to fix a bowl of porridge in company.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE, British slang for time in prison (and a TV sitcom), gives TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Done simultaneously or at once, a phrase meaning together in the sense of at the same moment.

clue.text: Backer provides a new stage, after reflection

indicators.note: reflection reverses a word as a mirror does, so the stage word is read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or contest

explanation.surface: A theatre sponsor funds a new stage after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' reads as careful thought, but it means mirroring, turning a word round.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatrical production.

clue.text: Problem of knotted ropes

indicators.note: knotted ropes are twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tangle of rope that presents a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or difficulty, a synonym of problem.

clue.text: Holy man from a Caribbean island

definitions.meaning: a friar of the order founded by St Dominic
belonging to Dominica, or to the Republic sharing Hispaniola

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Black Friar of St Dominic's order and a native of Dominica or its republican neighbour.

clue.text: See about wrong move with precision

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the See word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
X is the mark used for a wrong answer
to act is to take action, to make a move

explanation.surface: Looking closely at a mistaken step, carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a bishop's see: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly as an adverb means accurately or precisely, the same as with precision.

clue.text: Shocked when a good man's 'arrassed

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man in crosswords
harassed with its H dropped, as in Cockney speech, means hounded without its H

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned when a decent fellow is pestered, said in a dropped-H accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'arrassed signals a missing H, so harassed = HOUNDED becomes OUNDED; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounded means amazed or stunned, the same past-participle sense as shocked.

clue.text: Chance controlled Benedictine monk

parts.note: to run something is to control it, past tense ran
Dom is a title given to Benedictine monks

explanation.surface: By luck, a monk was in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Random as an adjective means by chance, unplanned; read as a modifier, 'chance' fits.

clue.text: Capture supporting position? That's the bottom line

parts.note: to net something is to capture it
pro means in favour of, supporting
to fit a part is to position it in place

explanation.surface: Taking a backing role? That is what really counts.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line of accounts shows final earnings after costs, the idiom behind the phrase.

clue.text: Alien used criminal in studies

parts.note: ET is the alien from the Spielberg film

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of used are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial used a lawbreaker in research.
explanation.definitionFit: Études are musical compositions written as studies to practise technique.

clue.text: Waste material that is in beastly disorder

parts.note: scrap is discarded or waste material
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Rubbish heaped in a filthy mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' is not a general insult: it means an illness of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep and goats, an animal ailment.

clue.text: Sinatra upset technician

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the singer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra annoyed a sound engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled craft worker, close to a technician in skill.

clue.text: Visual display of yellow in the atmosphere

indicators.note: in places the heraldic colour inside the atmosphere word

parts.note: an aura is the atmosphere surrounding a person or place
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A yellow glow seen in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the atmosphere' looks like where the display is, but THE ATMOSPHERE is AURA, holding OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aurora is a natural light show in polar skies, a visual display.

clue.text: Disgusting row about old man

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the row word goes around the old man piece

parts.note: a row is a din or noise
OM can stand for old man

explanation.surface: An argument about an elderly father turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or foul-smelling, a synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Aversion is new treatment in Alcoholics Anonymous

indicators.note: in places the treatment word inside the abbreviation of the support group

parts.note: use can mean treatment, as in ill use

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker's aversion to a new therapy at AA meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea can mean strong disgust or loathing, a figurative synonym of aversion.

clue.text: Married man who later rued arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A husband who regretted his affair afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who strays while wed is the kind of married man the noun names.

clue.text: Joint's connective tissue died away

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this reads 'a joint is'

indicators.note: away means taken off, so the died abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a tendon is connective tissue joining muscle to bone

explanation.surface: A joint's sinew has withered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests anatomy, as does connective tissue, but the joint is carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue of a mortise and tenon, a woodworking joint.

clue.text: Religious leader's endless chatter

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this reads 'a religious leader is'

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter

parts.note: to rabbit, in British slang, is to chatter on at length

explanation.surface: A cleric's never-ending prattle.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT (on) is British slang for talking endlessly, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher, the spiritual head of a congregation.

clue.text: Farm equipment used to get booze into Britain

indicators.note: into means the booze word goes inside the Britain abbreviation

parts.note: ale is beer, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: Machinery that is used to smuggle alcohol into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A baler is a machine that packs hay or straw into bales on a farm.

clue.text: Means of transport for Home Counties judoka

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE
a dan is a grade of black belt in judo, so a judoka of rank

explanation.surface: A car to take a judo expert around the commuter belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties bordering London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan is a covered chair carried on poles, and in America a saloon car.

clue.text: Briefcase left with page

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a folio is a leaf or page of a book

explanation.surface: A briefcase abandoned with a pageboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat case for carrying papers or drawings.

clue.text: Joiner takes money up front quite slowly

parts.note: and is a conjunction, a word that joins
an ante is a stake paid before play in poker

explanation.surface: A carpenter takes a deposit and works at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is a conjunction, AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Look round very fast

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the look word goes around the very abbreviation

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: Glancing about at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adverb for quickly, but it is the verb, going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, and to starve is to suffer from lack of it.
